topic: How can link budget calculations account for spatially variable SINR due to overlapping beams in a multigroup multicast precoding system?
consensus_response: To accurately account for spatially variable SINR due to overlapping beams, link budget calculations should consider the physical mechanism of array factor and interference patterns. The array factor's periodic function creates regions of constructive and destructive interference, affecting SINR. To mitigate this, beamforming optimization techniques can adjust antenna weights to minimize interference patterns. By incorporating Average Satisfaction Index (ASI) metrics into link budget calculations, designers can estimate the effect of overlapping beams on user throughput and overall system performance. Machine Learning-based beamforming optimization can further adapt beamforming weights and phase shifts based on historical data and real-time system performance, optimizing SINR and user throughput in dynamic environments.
reference_context: The reference context provides structured table data on Average Satisfaction Index (ASI) metrics, including Average Unmet System Capacity, Average Unused Offered Capacity, Average Used Carrier, Average Used Power, and Average Used Bandwidth. These metrics quantify the impact of overlapping beams on user satisfaction and can be incorporated into link budget calculations to estimate system performance.
